properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Raised 2026-08-28 from `fact:field-friction-is-captured-and-then-owed-to-nobody`, itself raised because three of four items in a field report said *"still true"* and *"same as 2026-08-18"*.

═══ THE PROBLEM IN ONE LINE ═══

Capture works. **190 defect-facts, 189 with nothing claiming to have answered them, 8 INVALIDATES edges in the whole design, and no `loop_status` debt class counts any of it.** A friction report enters the graph and the one call every session makes cannot see it.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) A NEW DEBT CLASS — `open_field_defects` on `loop_status`.** The obvious answer. ⚠️ Counter, and it is serious: **a count that can never reach zero becomes wallpaper**, and this project has already found that failure three times (`unreviewed_ideas` at 111 of 186, the undeclared-seam list, the unallocated-parts list). 189 rows on the orientation call would be ignored inside a week and would drown the seven numbers that currently mean something.

**(b) SCOPE IT THE WAY `unclaimed_findings` IS SCOPED.** That tool already solves the identical problem for a different question — it asks *"what did THIS SESSION make false?"* and returns a handful rather than hundreds, on the explicit reasoning that *"design-wide there are hundreds of open observations and a list that long is wallpaper."* The same trick may apply: not "all open field defects" but "field defects on ground you touched", or "reported more than once". ⭐ **This is the option with a working precedent inside the same codebase.**

**(c) MAKE REPETITION THE SIGNAL.** A friction item reported in two separate field reports is worth more than one reported once, and the second report is exactly when it becomes cheap to notice. Nothing today can tell that two reports describe the same item. ⚠️ Counter: needs the reports linked to their items, which is manual, and the reporter used placeholders (`cap:X`) precisely to avoid naming real nodes.

**(d) NOTHING NEW — USE `INVALIDATES` PROPERLY AND THE NUMBER FALLS.** Much of the 189 is surely fixed with nobody having drawn the edge. Sweeping and closing what is genuinely done might leave a backlog small enough to read without any new machinery. ⚠️ Counter: that is a one-time cleanup, not a mechanism; it will re-accumulate. ⭐ But it is the honest FIRST move regardless of which option follows, because **nobody knows how big the real backlog is** and every other option is being designed against a number that is a raw count rather than a measurement.

**(e) IT IS NOT REFLOW2'S JOB.** Bug triage belongs in an issue tracker, and this project has repeatedly refused to become one — the Task node type was killed on 2026-08-25 as *"the road to being a tracker"*. ⚠️ Counter: this is not tracking work, it is noticing that a recorded observation has gone unanswered — which is what `unclaimed_findings` and `invalidated_findings` already do. The line between them is real but thin, and worth stating rather than assuming.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT MUST BE MEASURED BEFORE CHOOSING ═══

**How many of the 189 are actually live?** The count is raw: `fact_type` is an optional free-string, so it both over- and under-counts, and an unknown share are fixed-but-unclosed. Designing a debt class against that number would be building for a backlog nobody has sized. **Option (d) is that measurement as well as a candidate remedy.**

📌 ADJACENT, NOT THE SAME: `fact:the-upstream-watch-is-findable-only-in-reflow2s-own-words` and `fact:a-findings-name-can-claim-more-than-its-data...` are both about a record being ACCURATE and still not reaching a reader. This one is about a record reaching nobody at all. Whether they are one problem — **the design writes faithfully and reads back selectively** — is itself unsettled.
properties.name: OPEN — what makes a field-reported defect OWED, when the loop counts structure and a friction report is a fact?
properties.rationale:
Raised because the repeats are the loudest signal in the report and have a different cause from the headline defect. Each repeated item has a local explanation and fixing all three would leave the pattern intact.

Filed against `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` because that rule makes field use the point, and field use produces exactly the input with no return path.

Option (d) is listed last among the doing-something options but flagged as the honest first move: every other option is being designed against a raw count, and nobody has sized the real backlog. Option (e) is a genuine option, not a strawman — this project has killed an adjacent idea for exactly that reason and the line deserves stating.
